summary: Python SDK streaming appears to hang (no tokens) and then raises timeout error; likely proxy buffering + streaming read-timeout defaults
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports that Python SDK streaming responses “hang” (no tokens emitted to their iterator) for ~30–90s and then fail with a timeout/transport error. Non-streaming requests succeed.

Impact
- User-facing chat feature intermittently fails in production for streaming mode.
- Customer is considering switching to non-streaming (degraded UX) or implementing a separate SSE client.

Customer report
- “When we stream, it looks like nothing happens, then we get a timeout. If we remove our corporate proxy or hit the endpoint from a laptop, it works.”

Environment
- Python 3.11
- redwood-sdk-python version: 0.9.2 (per customer)
- Network path: application -> corporate egress proxy (NGINX) -> Redwood Hosted API
- Region: us-east

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Run streaming chat completions behind their egress proxy.
2) Observe no partial tokens displayed; the process appears stuck.
3) After some time, SDK raises a timeout.

Expected
- Streaming iterator yields tokens/events continuously as they arrive.
- If the network path buffers data, SDK should either tolerate longer gaps between chunks for streaming or provide clear guidance/errors.

Actual
- No partial output for extended period, then timeout.

Error snippet (customer-provided)
- httpx.ReadTimeout: The read operation timed out
- (sometimes) httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected without sending a response

Additional notes
- Customer confirmed that direct connection (bypassing proxy) streams normally.
- Customer proxy config includes default buffering; they do not currently disable proxy buffering for event streams.
comments: 2025-01-14 10:22 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Created ticket based on customer escalation from CS. Requested: SDK version, traceback, and one failing request-id from response headers (if available) plus confirmation whether a proxy/WAF is in path.

2025-01-14 14:03 PT — Customer (Hearthside Analytics) — Confirmed python sdk v0.9.2. Proxy in path is NGINX-based egress proxy (managed by IT). Shared traceback showing httpx.ReadTimeout during streaming. Says: “Without proxy it streams; with proxy it stalls then times out.”

2025-01-15 09:11 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Initial hypothesis: proxy buffering is delaying delivery of SSE frames; Python SDK’s streaming read-timeout is firing due to lack of bytes for >N seconds. Asked customer to test (a) increased timeout (b) disabling proxy buffering for the route (c) curl --no-buffer to confirm buffering behavior.

2025-01-15 11:40 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Internal repro notes: using a buffering reverse proxy in front of SSE can delay small chunks until buffer flush thresholds. If the client has a finite per-read timeout, the read can time out while waiting for the proxy to flush. This matches the “hang then error” report. Non-streaming works because response completes within timeout.

Suggested customer experiment:
- Temporarily set streaming read timeout to None / very large.
- Ensure proxy disables buffering for event-stream responses (NGINX: proxy_buffering off; also check gzip / HTTP/2 buffering behavior).
- If possible, add a keepalive/heartbeat event from server (not currently guaranteed).

2025-01-16 08:27 PT — Customer (Hearthside Analytics) — Tested by bypassing proxy: streaming works and tokens arrive immediately. With proxy, no tokens for ~45s then timeout. IT can disable proxy buffering for specific upstreams but needs explicit guidance. Asked: “What headers/content-type should we key off of?”

2025-01-16 10:05 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Provided guidance: Redwood streaming uses Server-Sent Events (Content-Type: text/event-stream). Recommend configuring NGINX egress proxy to not buffer event streams (proxy_buffering off) and to avoid transformations (no content rewriting). Also recommended increasing client streaming timeout as immediate mitigation.

Python SDK workaround snippet (customer can apply now):
- Set a larger overall timeout and disable read timeout for streaming if their SDK version supports it.
- If not supported in v0.9.2, wrap with higher-level timeout and avoid aggressive per-read timeouts.

Also flagged internally to DevEx: streaming should not use small read timeout defaults; should align with SDK parity standard for streaming timeouts.

2025-01-17 13:18 PT — Ibrahim Khan (DevEx TL) — Confirmed this is consistent with items in the SDK parity audit: Python streaming currently inherits httpx read timeout defaults in some code paths. Plan: standardize streaming timeouts (connect finite; read disabled / very large; overall configurable) and improve error message to explicitly call out proxies/buffering when we detect ReadTimeout during SSE.

Tracking in:
- github:redwood-sdk-python#413 (timeouts)
- github:redwood-sdk-python#415 (streaming robustness)
- docs update in github:redwood-docs#904

2025-01-20 09:02 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Follow-up with customer: asked them to confirm whether setting NGINX proxy_buffering off for text/event-stream resolves the hang. Also asked for any remaining failures with request-id samples once changes are applied.

2025-01-21 16:37 PT — Customer (Hearthside Analytics) — Confirmed fix: disabling proxy buffering for Content-Type text/event-stream resolved the “hang then timeout” behavior. Streaming now delivers tokens continuously. Requested that Redwood docs explicitly mention proxy buffering and recommended timeout settings.

2025-01-21 17:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Marking Resolved. Resolution: customer-side proxy buffering was delaying SSE frames; Python SDK timed out waiting for bytes. Workaround implemented: disable buffering for event-stream in proxy + increase streaming timeout.

Next actions (internal):
- Ensure python sdk streaming defaults align with cross-SDK standard (read timeout disabled or sufficiently high for SSE).
- Add troubleshooting docs section for proxies and streaming (linked PR: github:redwood-docs#904).

No further action required for customer; will notify when SDK patch containing updated timeout defaults ships.
